Design choice: • All privileged actions are performed by IAM roles that assume SSM Session Manager permissions (AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore).  • No long‑lived SSH keys are stored on the Control Node.  • Cross‑account access uses resource‑based policies on the target accounts and AssumeRole chains, allowing a single set of AWS credentials on the Control Node.
Why it satisfies the requirement: • Eliminates secret leakage.  • Central governance – a change in a target account’s IAM policy instantly reflects for all roles.  • Scales to any number of accounts without redesign.

Design choice: • Tag‑based enrollment (monitoring=enabled).  • Dynamic inventory reads tags via amazon.aws.ec2_info.  • New VMs automatically qualify when the tag is added.
Why it satisfies the requirement: • No hard‑coded host lists → elastic.  • Tag‑driven model respects account boundaries – you can grant a specific account permission to self‑tag.

Design choice: • Run df -P / (or extended mount loop) on each VM.  • Parse and compute free %.  • Emit custom CloudWatch metrics (AWS/DiskMonitor).  • Optionally forward to a central OpenSearch index for cross‑account dashboards.
Why it satisfies the requirement: • Native AWS service → minimal agents, low overhead.  • Metrics are query‑able in real time for alerting.

Design choice: • All metrics live in CloudWatch (or OpenSearch) under a common namespace.  • Grafana (hosted on an EC2 or on Amazon Managed Grafana) connects to that store and renders a single dashboard with per‑account, per‑VM breakdowns.  • Dashboard panels include time‑series, heat‑maps, and “disk‑free %” gauges.
Why it satisfies the requirement: • One‑stop view across accounts.  • Easy to add new visualization widgets (e.g., top‑10 full disks).

Design choice: • Dynamic inventory automatically adds new accounts/V​Ms when they are tagged.  • Ansible playbooks are idempotent – re‑running them is safe.  • Metrics are stateless; no local state is persisted on the Control Node.  • Horizontal scaling of the Control Node (e.g., run multiple parallel playbook executions) or use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate large fleets.
Why it satisfies the requirement: • Adding accounts = just add a new entry to accounts.yml and grant the required IAM role.  • Per‑run concurrency can be tuned (e.g., forks: 20) to keep API‑rate limits in check.

Design choice: • All traffic between Control Node and VMs goes through SSM (TLS‑encrypted).  • Metric values never contain credentials – they are signed with temporary STS tokens.  • Secrets (e.g., OpenSearch password) are stored in AWS Secrets Manager and fetched at runtime.
Why it satisfies the requirement: • Meets compliance (no static passwords).  • Auditable – access logs are captured in CloudTrail.
